panels.title: The citadel above its harbour
panels.desc: The Citadel of Iron Quorums on its height, the sea wall with its tide marks below, ships at the harbour under the walls.
panels.scene: High three-quarter view of the citadel crowning its headland, crenellated walls and towers above the sea wall and harbour. On the wall, numbered tablets are pinned between the carved low-tide and high-tide lines. Below, a squadron rides at anchor and keepers move along the wall-walk.

panels.title: The inquisitors arrive
panels.desc: Two stern inquisitors step off a ship at the harbour below the citadel, one with an abacus and ledger, the other with builder's plans; the half-built citadel rises on the hill above.
panels.scene: Two stern inquisitors in dark travelling cloaks step off a ship onto the quay below the citadel, one carrying an abacus and a thick ledger of accounts, the other a set of builder's plans. Above them on the height rises the half-built citadel with scaffolding; in the distance, sketched thin, stand two older rival fortifications, over-ornate and crumbling.
panels.caption: THE INQUISITORS SAILED IN NOT WITH A NEW THEOREM, BUT WITH A BUDGET.

panels.title: The siege by delay
panels.desc: At night outside the citadel gate, saboteurs quietly obstruct honest messengers while keepers inside cross an absent keeper's name off a roster.
panels.scene: At night outside the citadel gate, cloaked saboteurs quietly obstruct honest messengers — one tangles a messenger's horse's reins, another sends a messenger down the wrong road with a false signpost. Inside the gate, keepers staring at a sundial are crossing an absent keeper's name off a roster, while the real traitor among them smiles.
panels.caption: THE SIEGE BY DELAY: IF A FORTRESS EXPELS WHOEVER IS SLOW, THE ENEMY NEED NOT BRIBE THE HONEST — ONLY SLOW THEM DOWN.

panels.title: Four keepers, one warden
panels.desc: In a torch-lit vault, four keepers stand around a great iron-bound chest, each with a key; in the shadows, a pirate's hand slips a bribe to one of them.
panels.scene: Inside a torch-lit vault within the citadel, four keepers in bronze-studded leather stand around a great iron-bound treasure chest, each holding one of four keys; one keeper (the warden) wears a chain of office. In the shadows behind one of the ordinary keepers, a pirate's hand slips a bag of coins into his belt, unseen by the others.
panels.cast: four keepers, an unseen pirate hand
panels.caption: FOUR KEEPERS, ONE WARDEN — AND ANY ONE OF THEM MIGHT BE IN THE PIRATES’ PAY.

panels.title: The three-phase gauntlet
panels.desc: Along the citadel's inner wall: the warden nails up a proposal, the keepers each nail a matching token, and at last all ring their bells and the chest is unlocked.
panels.scene: A three-stage scene along the inner wall of the citadel. Stage one: the warden nails a small tablet bearing a number and a wax impression to a gatepost. Stage two: three keepers each nail a matching token beside it and send runners to the others. Stage three: all keepers ring small bronze bells in unison, and a clerk finally unlocks the treasure chest.
panels.caption: THE THREE-PHASE GAUNTLET: THE WARDEN PROPOSES, THE KEEPERS CONFIRM THEY ALL HEARD THE SAME THING — AND THEN CONFIRM THAT ENOUGH OF THEM KNOW IT.

panels.title: The census of the vault
panels.desc: On the sea wall below the citadel: keepers pull down numbered tablets below the low-tide line and toss them to the sea once enough seals agree.
panels.scene: The sea wall below the citadel, carved with a low-tide line and a high-tide line; between them, numbered tablets are pinned to the wall. A team of keepers pulls down all the tablets below the low-tide line and tosses them into the sea, while one keeper holds up a counting-board stamped with matching seals.
panels.caption: ONCE 2F + 1 KEEPERS SEAL THE SAME COUNT, EVERYTHING BELOW THE LOW-TIDE MARK MAY BE THROWN INTO THE SEA.

panels.title: The new warden
panels.desc: At dawn in the citadel courtyard, keepers lift the chain of office from a silent warden; the next in rotation receives it and stamps a blank tablet where nothing was prepared.
panels.scene: In the citadel courtyard at dawn, three keepers stand before a slumped, silent warden and lift the chain of office from his neck. The next keeper in the rotation receives the chain and unrolls a long scroll assembled from bundles of sealed tokens that the others hand him; in a gap in the scroll he stamps a blank tablet marked only with a circle.
panels.cast: the deposed warden, the new warden, keepers
panels.caption: THE NEW WARDEN MAY NOT FORGET WHAT HIS PREDECESSOR’S KEEPERS PREPARED. WHERE NOTHING WAS PREPARED, HE WRITES A BLANK.

panels.title: The budget
panels.desc: A still-life comparison: a heavy signet ring and bubbling wax beside a nearly-spent hourglass, against a bundle of split tally sticks beside one barely started.
panels.scene: An illustrative still-life, not a place on the island. Left: a heavy gold signet ring beside a pot of bubbling red wax, a sweating scribe, and a large hourglass nearly run out. Right: a bundle of notched wooden tally sticks, each split lengthwise into two matching halves, with a small hourglass that has barely started.
panels.caption: THE BUDGET: A SIGNET SEAL PROVES YOUR WORD TO ANYONE, SLOWLY. A SPLIT TALLY PROVES IT TO ONE PARTNER, A THOUSAND TIMES FASTER.

panels.title: The trial of the five labours
panels.desc: Two libraries race side by side: an ordinary open one, and a fortified one guarded by four keepers, an identical scribe working in each while a judge watches.
panels.scene: An illustrative scene, not a place on the island. A race between two libraries side by side. On the left, an ordinary open library where one scribe performs five labours in sequence (building shelves, copying scrolls, checking labels, reading every line, binding codices). On the right, a fortified library with four keepers at a gate checking every scroll, where an identical scribe performs the same five labours. A judge with an hourglass watches; the fortified scribe is only a half-step behind.
panels.cast: two scribes, a judge, four keepers
panels.caption: THE TRIAL OF THE FIVE LABOURS: WITH FOUR KEEPERS AND ONE POSSIBLE TRAITOR, THE GUARDED LIBRARY FINISHED ONLY 3% BEHIND THE CITY’S ORDINARY ONE.
